Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-polish-medium-0021", "row_sha256": "0278616b5b86f9838f4e838cb5580700b504f5e03c86f80cfac2dc5758407721", "mode": "/polish", "language": "en", "context": {"profile": "Clear and professional."}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Rewrite awkward phrasing into readable prose for the supplied profile, or plain prose when none is supplied. Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "we're preparing the next screen-reader audit for the account settings flow, and I need a short review note for the design and engineering teams. The review is for the notification preference controls and the save status message, not the rest of the settings flow. Please do the audit with keyboard navigation and a screen reader. For each control, note what the screen reader announces, and record the setting you changed and whether you navigated to it by keyboard. Also check whether the save status is announced after a change. If the controls are announced with their name, current state, and available action, and the save status is conveyed after a change, record that these checks passed and leave the existing labels and status behavior unchanged. If either control's information is missing or the save status is not announced after a change, list the specific item and recommend the smallest wording or interaction adjustment that would make it available to screen-reader users. Keep the two findings separate and identify which check triggered any recommendation. Don't treat a visual highlight by itself as proof that the state was announced. The note should distinguish what you observed during testing from any proposed adjustment, so the team can decide what to change after reviewing the evidence. Please don't make changes during the audit; we're asking for findings and recommendations only.", "output": "We’re preparing the next screen-reader audit for the account settings flow and need a short review note for the design and engineering teams. The review covers the notification preference controls and the save status message, not the rest of the settings flow. Please conduct the audit using keyboard navigation and a screen reader. For each control, note what the screen reader announces, the setting you changed, and whether you navigated to it by keyboard. Also check whether the save status is announced after a change.

If the controls are announced with their name, current state, and available action, and the save status is conveyed after a change, record that these checks passed and leave the existing labels and status behavior unchanged. If either control’s information is missing or the save status is not announced after a change, list the specific item and recommend the smallest wording or interaction adjustment that would make it available to screen-reader users. Keep the two findings separate and identify which check prompted any recommendation. A visual highlight alone does not prove that the state was announced.

Distinguish what you observed during testing from any proposed adjustment so the team can decide what to change after reviewing the evidence. Please don’t make changes during the audit; we’re asking for findings and recommendations only."}]
